## Findings 2026-10-28 20:05–20:40 PDT

**The plateau metric is not process RSS.** `infra/scripts/observability.sh` publishes `docker stats` MemUsage as `container_memory_rss_bytes` / `memory_rss_bytes`, parsed from Docker's rounded display string, so "2.5GiB" logs as exactly 2,684,354,560. On cgroup v2 that figure is the container's memory charge minus inactive file cache, so it includes active page cache. The metric name overstates what it measures, and its 2–3 significant figures hide small changes.

**But this time the memory was the process's own.** Sampling the new container's cgroup `memory.stat` every 5 minutes after the 20:16 PDT redeploy:

| PDT | docker usage | anon | active+inactive file | process RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20:17 | 64 MiB | 60.5 MB | 35 MB | 75 MB |
| 20:22 | 733 MiB | 544 MB | 147 MB | 561 MB |
| 20:27 | 773 MiB | 583 MB | 141 MB | 599 MB |
| 20:32 | 794 MiB | 583 MB | 171 MB | 600 MB |
| 20:37 | — | 583 MB | — | — |

The only work between 20:17 and 20:22 was one completion-verify gate job (keepalive log: precheck 20:21:39, search_files tool call 20:22:05, verify step complete 20:22:42 after 56 s). The job finished, 3 threads remain, and 583 MB of anonymous memory stayed resident afterwards. By contrast, 9 concurrent `next_batch` calls in the same image return their memory when they finish (see teenage-unquieted-ringworm).

**Not import cost.** In the same image, importing `rebar.mcp_server`, the completion and plan-review gate modules, `boto3` and `anthropic` brings RSS to 73 MB.

**Ruled out by reading:** both pinned-ticket-view owners close their view (`close_precheck._completion_precheck` in a `finally`, `completion.verify_completion` via `owns_ticket_view`).

**Next:** run the completion gate 3 times in one process inside the MCP image against an isolated store clone, recording RSS after each run, to tell a per-run leak (grows each time) from a one-time cache (one step, then flat).
